newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific vows to pursue Pennzoil.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific vows to pursue Pennzoil.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said the rejection of its hostile, $4.2 billion bid for Pennzoil Co by that company's board offered nothing new to shareholders.

"UPR is disappointed but unsurprised by the board's response. The business rationale of this combination is so powerful, and the premium we are offering shareholders so substantial, that we believe the merger of UPR and Pennzoil is inevitable," Union Pacific Resources said in a statement.
Pennzoil's board earlier rejected the bid, saying that it could deliver better value to shareholders than the $84-per-share cash and stock offer, which Union Pacific made last week.

Pennzoil disputes that the offer is worth $84, as Union Pacific would pay for a little less than half of the total with its shares, which are trading at $25 each. That is the bottom end of the pricing collar on which Union Pacific based the value of its transaction.
However, Union Pacific accused Pennzoil's management of building in "virtually zero value," noting that its shares have fallen 33 percent from 1990 to the day before the offer.
It said Pennzoil had squandered a $3.0 billion payout from Texaco as settlement from litigation.
Pennzoil says that after tax, the proceeds of that payout were $2.2 billion, and part of that was eventually swapped with Chevron Corp for the same overseas properties that Union Pacific now covets.

Union Pacific said its offer would deliver "present" value to shareholders, not "speculative" value. The present value is substantially above what Pennzoil is promising "four to five years from now," it said. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
